text.p: Jacques Kallis scored 82 to help South Africa reach 221 for eight in 50 overs after Adam Dale had taken three quick wickets in the second of seven one-day internationals at St. George's Park on Monday.

Mark Taylor had no hesitation in putting South Africa in to bat on a green wicket under overcast skies and 28-year-old Queensland fast bowler Dale, in his second game, quickly reduced the home side to 16 for three in eight overs.
Dale had local debutant Louis Koen caught at second slip for a duck, Adam Bacher caught at mid off for three and then bowled Daryll Cullinan for another duck.
But Kallis and Jonty Rhodes added 104 for the fourth wicket to rescue the innings with Rhodes scampering quick singles and Kallis launching Shane Warne for a towering six over square leg.
Rhodes drove a tame catch to mid on to depart for 57 from 86 balls with seven fours but Kallis and Hansie Cronje (31) added another 61 for the fifth wicket to mainatin the recovery.
Cronje and Kallis were both bowled by Jason Gillespie in the 45th over with Kallis making his fifth half century in his 20th match. His 82 came from 118 balls with five fours and the six.
Strangely, Dale was not brought back into the attack after his first seven overs which included three maidens and earned him three wickets for just 18 runs.

The game started inauspiciously for Australia when the two teams lined up for the playing of the respective national anthems. While South enjoyed Nkosi Sikele i'Africa, Australia had to endure Waltzing Matilda and not Advance Australia Fair after a mi-up in tapes.
